why: The first values in the trace are right, but the student uses a rule that goes against Java: a variable that already has a value keeps it when you assign to it again. So total stays 11.5, when the last line actually changes it to 12.42.

concepts.quote: after the last line total is still 11.5, because it already has a value.
concepts.why: Assigning to a double variable replaces what it holds: total + total * TAX stores 12.42.

concepts.quote: total is still 11.5, because it already has a value
concepts.why: total = total + ... reads total, works out the new amount and stores it back, so the value changes.
The result of a * 2 + 1.5 is right, but there is no reasoning showing that the int a * 2 gets widened to double.
